newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran radio attacks UK, U.S. for meddling in Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Iran radio attacks UK, U.S. for meddling in Gulf.

text.p: Iran accused Britain and the United States of meddling in the Gulf and said interference by the two Western powers was preventing cooperation between countries of the region.

"Despite the desire of all the Moslem nations in the Persian Gulf -- and, in some cases, certain regional governments -- what has been, and is, preventing cooperation and consultation between Persian Gulf countries, is the influence and interference of foreign powers, such as Britain and America, in the region," Iranian state radio said on Sunday.
Britain and the United States maintain armed forces in the Gulf.

The radio, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, said in a commentary the meddling and divisive presence of foreigners in the region had caused various misunderstandings and, at times, had allowed opportunist countries to invade their neighbours.
This was the result of a lack of unanimity among regional countries on issues of common interest and the inability to distinguish them from the interests of foreigners, it said.

"This has paved the way for instability and has forced those countries, in order to reduce their suffering as a result of existing hardships, to seek the necessary backing from outside the region," it added.
"Under such circumstances, consultation between regional countries, including what has taken place between Iran and Qatar, is necessary," the radio said.
The commentary followed a one-day visit to Tehran by the foreign minister of the Gulf Arab state of Qatar, Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani.

Sheikh Hamad was reported by the official Iranian news agency IRNA on Saturday as saying at a meeting with President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani that Iran was important in maintaining peace and security in the Gulf.
Qatar is a member of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) which has accused Iran of interfering in the affairs of states on the Arab side of the waterway, a charge denied by Tehran.
The GCC also includes Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Oman.

The group's annual summit in December called on Iran to end its occupation of three Gulf islands claimed by the UAE and also criticised Tehran's deployment of surface-to-surface missiles in the region.
